steps.text: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat; stir in onion, flour, salt, and white pepper. Stir in half-and-half and chicken broth; cook, stirring frequently, at medium heat until thickened. Off heat, stir in thyme and cayenne pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Bechamel Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This bechamel sauce recipe makes a creamy white sauce with chicken broth, cream, butter, and flour flavored with grated onion, white pepper, and thyme.
raw_recipe.name: Bechamel Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat; stir in onion, flour, salt, and white pepper. Stir in half-and-half and chicken broth; cook, stirring frequently, at medium heat until thickened. Off heat, stir in thyme and cayenne pepper.

review.reviewBody: I use this often in lasagna. Instead of the cream and broth, I use 2 cups milk and a bouillon cube. Sometimes I'll also add in some grated emmental or parmesan cheese.

This recipe was EXCELLENT and very, very easy. I followed it to a T, but after it thickened and I removed it from the stove I added some shredded white cheddar - YUM. Any time I need a white sauce for anything, this is the recipe I'll be using.

Our family really enjoyed this. I appreciated how easy it was to make.

I chose to use the stovetop method. The changes that I made were these: 1) Instead of grating the onion, I minced it to maintain the full flavor and used 3 Tbsp instead of two. 2) Then I melted only 1/2 of the butter in the pan and sautéed the onions in that. Then I tossed in the other half of the butter and let that melt before adding the flour. 3) I didn't have half-n-half or cream on hand, so I used 1 C. Of 2% milk and an extra tablespoon of butter (I added the milk and butter at the same time and didn't bother softening or melting the pat in advance.) 

And finally--not really a change to the sauce recipe, but rather a "serving suggestion"--I stirred last night's leftover, baked salmon (flaked) into the sauce about 1 minute prior to serving it all over linguine. Delicious!

Great recipe! I've made it a couple of times and it's turned out great both times. I never have half-and-half, so I use 1/2 c. heavy cream and 1/2 c. skim milk and it turns out wonderfully. I also use black pepper instead of white. Last time I added in some red bell pepper and red onion I cooked with no oil on a nonstick skillet, and it turned out very pretty and tasted great!

I think this is an excellent version of bechamel. Prior to this recipe I'd never tried one that included chicken broth, which lightens up the calories a bit, but I discovered I quite liked it. I wrote down the stovetop method (and that's what I used) but the recipe doesn't instruct you to use any of the seasonings if you follow those directions so be sure to write down ALL the ingredients. Mine came out fine because I was adding a different seasoning anyway. I would also advise you NOT to add all the cold liquid at once -- that's the best way known to make lumpy sauces/gravies. Instead add a bit, whisk it smooth, then add a bit more, whisk again, etc. til you've added it all. Thanks for the recipe! P.S. I tested this recipe with fat-free half & half and it came out great. You could make this with skim milk too, just cook and stir til it reaches the right thickness.

This is absolutely my favourite bechamel sauce. I use it with any "au gratin", with pasta and in lasagna. I didn't have half and half and didn't like the idea of chicken broth making my sauce brown, so I used 2 cups of milk instead. I also added the seasoning in while it was cooking, and it was so good that I do it that way every time. I also add some grated cheddar cheese in the end when I use it in an "au gratin". DELICIOUS!

I made this sauce for my salmon pie. Made it exactly as written. Very nice creamy texture and the taste adds to my salmon pie. I am very happy with this recipe. I did add to the sauce ,some cut up hard boiled eggs and 2 tablespoons of chopped pimentos, which gave it color and a old fashion flavor memory for me. You won't be disappointed using this recipe.

Just made this and it turned out really well. Not too heavy, but still rich in flavor. I did add some garlic and because I made it for a carbonara dish, I also added a cup of shredded parmesan and romano cheese. That really kicked it up a notch. I just found my new recipe for white sauce :)

Good recipe for a white sauce and you don't have Parmesan cheese in your fridge. Omitted half the butter for olive oil and instead flour I used 2 egg yolks for the amount of Flour needed. I read half-half used regular milk and sour cream (added honey to cut acidity). Came out really tasty and creamy enough

Good sauce however, substituted thyme with 1 large bay leaf (thyme can be overpowering for some dishes) and the broth/half-and-half with 2 cups whole milk. Omitted salt (used salted butter) and made a light blonde rue with the butter and flour, created just a bit more character. This recipe is a great starting point for many other sauces. With the addition of other herbs/spices/cheeses you can go to mornay sauce, bernaise sauce and many ohters.

Made on stovetop and sautéed onions in butter in beg. Did add white pepper (not my fav) and all spices with flour to thicken to liquid. Also added some white wine and loved the result. Tho will not (pers pref) add white pepper next time. Very good sauce !
This worked PERFECTLY with the chicken breast and spiral pasta we just had for dinner. Great, simple recipe!
I used this sauce in my Farfalle Pasta with Ham and Peas. Instead of chicken broth, I used Bone Broth and it was absolutely perfect.
I use this sauce in my lasagne and it works beautifully I use dried onion flakes in place of grated onion, add a pinch of nutmeg, and add grated cheese when thickened. Turns out perfectly.
I loved this sauce. Has a very delicate yet savory flavor. A keeper for sure.
This is probably my 6x making this particular recipe I substituted The Cayenne pepper for a smoke paprika to bring down the spice
Loved it. Very easy to make!
This was like I used to eat in Sicily on top of lasagna years ago ,great.

I made this in order to help with some chicken I had made yesterday and put a bit too much spice in! I used chicken broth, half and half, flour, onion powder, garlic powder, and ditalini pasta as well as the aforementioned chicken. I feel that this recipe was great inspiration and it turned what ended up falling far below the mark with how much spice I added to it yesterday and this something that was really really good today!
I made this gluten free using rice flour, I added one extra tbs of rice flour other than that flowers the recipe to a T was great
